newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end narrowly mixed, trade main seller.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end narrowly mixed, trade main seller.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed narrowly mixed as speculative buying ahead of the close lifted prices off the lows, dealers said.

Trade selling kept the most-active May contract below unchanged, however. The contract ended 1.95 cents lower at 81.85 cents per pound, traded 83.90 to 81.55 cents. Spot March closed down 2.10 at 79.05 cents.
Volume was estimated at 6,000 lots compared with Friday's official volume of 4,901 lots.
Dealers said the funds rolled short positions from March into May, tightening the spread to a 1.95 premium in May from a 2.80 premium on Friday. March 3 is the first notice day for the spot month.

Open interest in March remained high at 7,355 lots. The market will focus on delivery notices and liquidating open interest in March throughout the week, Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter said.
Open interest in May rose 601 lots to 10,507 lots.
"We should start seeing more spread activity but the focus will also be on cash prices," Georgakis added.
Ample supplies and weak demand is likely to keep futures prices under pressure, analysts said. Florida remains poised to produce a record 220 million 90-lb boxes, in 1996/97.
Support in May was seen at the recent low of 77.50 cents.
